# QA Automation Engineer Roadmap

> Ensure software quality through intelligent testing

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/qa-automation

QA Automation engineers design test strategies, write automated tests, and ensure software works flawlessly before it reaches users.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Moderate |
| Time to job-ready | 6-10 months to job-ready |
| Demand | High |
| Salary (India) | ₹4-12 LPA (entry) → ₹15-35 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $50K-75K (entry) → $100K-160K+ (senior) |
| Growth | Strong — shift-left testing and DevOps integration are increasing demand for automation engineers. |

## Required skills

- Selenium/Cypress/Playwright
- Python/Java/JS
- Test Frameworks
- API Testing
- CI/CD
- Performance Testing
- SQL

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (1-2 months)

- **Testing Fundamentals** — Test types, strategies, STLC, bug lifecycle
- **Programming** — Python or JavaScript for test scripting
- **Manual Testing** — Test cases, scenarios, exploratory testing

Resources:

- ISTQB Foundation
- Test Automation University
- Ministry of Testing

Projects:

- Write test cases for a web app
- Bug report documentation
- Test plan creation

### Phase 2: Core Skills (2-3 months)

- **Selenium/Playwright** — Browser automation, locators, waits, POM
- **API Testing** — Postman, REST Assured, API automation
- **Test Frameworks** — pytest, TestNG, Jest — structure and reporting

Resources:

- Selenium docs
- Playwright docs
- Postman Learning Center

Projects:

- E-commerce test suite
- API test automation
- Cross-browser testing

### Phase 3: Advanced Testing (2-3 months)

- **CI/CD Integration** — Run tests in pipelines, GitHub Actions
- **Performance Testing** — JMeter, k6, load testing
- **Mobile Testing** — Appium basics, responsive testing

Resources:

- JMeter docs
- k6 docs
- Appium docs

Projects:

- Pipeline-integrated test suite
- Performance test report
- Mobile test framework

### Phase 4: Projects (1-2 months)

- **Framework Design** — Build a reusable test automation framework
- **Real-World Testing** — Test open-source or volunteer projects
- **Documentation** — Test strategies, reports, metrics

Resources:

- GitHub
- Open source projects
- Testing blogs

Projects:

- Complete automation framework
- Test coverage analysis
- Quality metrics dashboard

### Phase 5: Job Preparation (1 month)

- **Portfolio** — Showcase test frameworks and strategies
- **Certifications** — ISTQB, cloud testing certs
- **Interview Prep** — Testing scenarios, coding challenges

Resources:

- Glassdoor
- LinkedIn
- Testing communities

Projects:

- Polish GitHub repos
- Mock interviews
- Networking

## Reality check

QA is sometimes undervalued, but great QA engineers are worth their weight in gold. The role is evolving rapidly — automation skills are now non-negotiable.

## What a QA Automation Engineer actually does day to day

QA Automation engineers design test strategies, write automated tests, and ensure software works flawlessly before it reaches users. In practice the week looks less like continuous coding and more like a mix of building, reviewing, debugging and deciding. A typical day includes a short stand-up, two to four hours of focused build time, code review for teammates, and at least one conversation about scope or trade-offs. The people who progress fastest in this role are the ones who treat those conversations as part of the job rather than as an interruption to it.

- **Morning:** triage anything that broke overnight, then take the highest-leverage task rather than the easiest one.
- **Core hours:** deep work on the current increment — Selenium/Cypress/Playwright, Python/Java/JS and Test Frameworks are the tools you will touch most.
- **Reviews:** reading other people's changes is the fastest way to learn a codebase and the fastest way to build trust.
- **Documentation:** a short written note about why a decision was made saves hours for the next person, often you in three months.
- **Learning:** the field moves; an hour a week on fundamentals beats a weekend binge every quarter.

## Is QA Automation Engineer the right fit for you?

This path suits you if several of the following are true. It is worth being honest here — switching after six months costs far more than choosing carefully now.

- You have a keen eye for detail and edge cases
- You enjoy breaking things to make them better
- You're methodical and thorough
- You care deeply about quality and reliability

> **Honest difficulty:** QA is sometimes undervalued, but great QA engineers are worth their weight in gold. The role is evolving rapidly — automation skills are now non-negotiable. Competition is rated medium and the entry barrier low, with realistic time to job-ready around 6-10 months (entry) → 2-3 years (expert).

## QA Automation Engineer salary in 2027

Compensation for qa automation engineers reflects scope more than years served. Strong — shift-left testing and DevOps integration are increasing demand for automation engineers. The bands below are annual gross figures; product companies pay above them, services and agency employers below.

QA Automation Engineer salary bands, 2027

| Level | Experience | India | Global (USD) | What the role owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry / junior | 0–2 years | ₹4-12 LPA (entry) | $50K-75K (entry) | Well-scoped tasks with close review |
| Mid-level | 3–5 years | Between the entry and senior bands | Between the entry and senior bands | Owns features end to end, mentors juniors |
| Senior | 6+ years | ₹15-35 LPA (senior) | $100K-160K+ (senior) | Owns systems, sets technical direction |
| Lead / staff | 9+ years | Above the senior band, plus equity at product companies | Above the senior band, plus equity | Leverage through other engineers and architecture |

Three factors move you up these bands faster than time does: specialising in one high-demand area rather than staying general, owning a system end to end so you can describe impact in numbers, and changing employer at the right moment — external moves still outpace internal raises in most markets. Use the [salary predictor](https://www.skillta.tech/salary-predictor) to check the band for your specific city and experience level.

## The complete QA Automation Engineer skill map

You need 7 core competencies to be credible in interviews for this role. The table maps each one to why employers care and how it gets tested, so you can prioritise instead of trying to learn everything at once.

Core QA Automation Engineer skills and how they are assessed

| Skill | Why it matters | How interviewers test it | Time to proficiency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selenium/Cypress/Playwright | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Deep questions about a project on your CV | 4–8 weeks |
| Python/Java/JS | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Deep questions about a project on your CV | 4–8 weeks |
| Test Frameworks | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 2–3 months |
| API Testing | Appears in the majority of job descriptions for this role | Deep questions about a project on your CV | 2–3 months |
| CI/CD | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |
| Performance Testing | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Debugging a broken example | 2–3 months |
| SQL | Most common source of production incidents when done badly | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |

The roadmap phases above tell you what to learn. This plan tells you when, assuming 10–15 hours a week of focused study. Slipping a week is normal; skipping the build column is not — the projects are what make the learning stick and what fills your portfolio.

Week-by-week QA Automation Engineer study plan (10–15 hours a week)

| Weeks 11–12 | Phase 2: Core Skills | Test Frameworks — pytest, TestNG, Jest — structure and reporting | Cross-browser testing |
| Weeks 13–14 | Phase 3: Advanced Testing | CI/CD Integration — Run tests in pipelines, GitHub Actions | Pipeline-integrated test suite |
| Weeks 15–16 | Phase 3: Advanced Testing | Performance Testing — JMeter, k6, load testing | Performance test report |
| Weeks 17–18 | Phase 3: Advanced Testing | Mobile Testing — Appium basics, responsive testing | Mobile test framework |
| Weeks 19–20 | Phase 4: Projects | Framework Design — Build a reusable test automation framework | Complete automation framework |
| Weeks 21–22 | Phase 4: Projects | Real-World Testing — Test open-source or volunteer projects | Test coverage analysis |
| Weeks 23–24 | Phase 4: Projects | Documentation — Test strategies, reports, metrics | Quality metrics dashboard |
| Weeks 25–26 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Portfolio — Showcase test frameworks and strategies | Polish GitHub repos |
| Weeks 27–28 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Certifications — ISTQB, cloud testing certs | Mock interviews |
| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Interview Prep — Testing scenarios, coding challenges | Networking |

## Portfolio projects that get interviews

Recruiters skim portfolios in under a minute, so two strong projects beat six weak ones. Each project below should be deployed, documented with a short README explaining the problem and the trade-offs, and something you can talk through for ten minutes without notes.

1. Write test cases for a web app
2. Bug report documentation
3. Test plan creation
4. E-commerce test suite
5. API test automation
6. Cross-browser testing
7. Pipeline-integrated test suite
8. Performance test report
9. Mobile test framework
10. Complete automation framework

Make at least one project unmistakably yours — solve a problem you actually have, use real data, and write up what broke. Interviewers ask far better questions about original work than about a cloned tutorial app, and those questions are the ones you will answer best.

# Mobile App Developer Roadmap

> Build apps that live in everyone's pocket

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/mobile-developer

Mobile developers create iOS and Android applications. From social apps to fintech, mobile is where billions of users interact with technology daily.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Moderate |
| Time to job-ready | 8-12 months to job-ready |
| Demand | High |
| Salary (India) | ₹4-14 LPA (entry) → ₹18-45 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $55K-85K (entry) → $120K-200K+ (senior) |
| Growth | Strong — mobile usage continues to grow. Cross-platform frameworks are making it easier to target both platforms. |

## Required skills

- React Native/Flutter/Swift/Kotlin
- UI Design
- State Management
- APIs
- App Store Deployment
- Testing
- Performance

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (2-3 months)

- **Choose Your Path** — React Native (JS), Flutter (Dart), or Native (Swift/Kotlin)
- **Programming Language** — Master JS/Dart/Swift/Kotlin
- **UI Basics** — Layouts, navigation, components

Resources:

- React Native docs
- Flutter docs
- Apple/Android dev docs

Projects:

- Calculator app
- Weather app
- Notes app

### Phase 2: Core Skills (2-3 months)

- **State Management** — Redux/Provider/Riverpod/SwiftUI state
- **API Integration** — REST APIs, JSON parsing, authentication
- **Navigation** — Complex navigation patterns, deep linking

Resources:

- Flutter cookbook
- React Navigation docs
- API tutorials

Projects:

- Social feed app
- E-commerce app
- Chat application

### Phase 3: Advanced Features (2-3 months)

- **Local Storage** — SQLite, AsyncStorage, Hive
- **Push Notifications** — FCM, APNs, notification handling
- **Performance** — Profiling, optimization, lazy loading

Resources:

- Firebase docs
- Performance optimization guides
- Platform-specific docs

Projects:

- Offline-first app
- Real-time messaging
- Media-heavy app

### Phase 4: Deployment (1-2 months)

- **App Store Submission** — iOS App Store and Google Play Store
- **CI/CD for Mobile** — Fastlane, CodePush, automated builds
- **Analytics** — Firebase Analytics, crash reporting

Resources:

- App Store guidelines
- Fastlane docs
- Firebase

Projects:

- Publish an app
- Set up CI/CD
- Analytics dashboard

### Phase 5: Job Preparation (1 month)

- **Portfolio Apps** — 2-3 polished apps on stores
- **Open Source** — Contribute to mobile libraries
- **Interview Prep** — Mobile-specific questions, system design

Resources:

- LeetCode
- Mobile dev communities
- YouTube

Projects:

- Polish portfolio
- Blog about mobile dev
- Mock interviews

| Weeks 25–26 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Portfolio Apps — 2-3 polished apps on stores | Polish portfolio |
| Weeks 27–28 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Open Source — Contribute to mobile libraries | Blog about mobile dev |
| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Interview Prep — Mobile-specific questions, system design | Mock interviews |

## Portfolio projects that get interviews

Recruiters skim portfolios in under a minute, so two strong projects beat six weak ones. Each project below should be deployed, documented with a short README explaining the problem and the trade-offs, and something you can talk through for ten minutes without notes.

1. Calculator app
2. Weather app
3. Notes app
4. Social feed app
5. E-commerce app
6. Chat application
7. Offline-first app
8. Real-time messaging
9. Media-heavy app
10. Publish an app

Make at least one project unmistakably yours — solve a problem you actually have, use real data, and write up what broke. Interviewers ask far better questions about original work than about a cloned tutorial app, and those questions are the ones you will answer best.

## Free resources worth using

- React Native docs
- Flutter docs
- Apple/Android dev docs
- Flutter cookbook
- React Navigation docs
- API tutorials
- Firebase docs
- Performance optimization guides
- Platform-specific docs
- App Store guidelines
- Fastlane docs
- Firebase
- LeetCode
- Mobile dev communities
- YouTube

Pick one primary resource and one reference. Rotating between five courses feels productive and teaches very little; finishing one and building alongside it teaches a lot. Official documentation should become your default reference within the first two months.

## Mobile App Developer interview preparation

Interview loops for this role typically run four to six stages. Expect a recruiter screen, a technical screen on fundamentals, a practical exercise or take-home, a deep-dive on your own projects, and a hiring-manager conversation about ownership and collaboration.

| Round | What is tested | Preparation that works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Motivation, communication, salary alignment | A 90-second summary of your work and a researched range |
| Technical fundamentals | React Native/Flutter/Swift/Kotlin, UI Design and State Management | Daily reps for four weeks, explained out loud |
| Practical exercise | Code quality, tests, judgement about scope | Timebox it and document what you deliberately left out |
| Project deep-dive | Whether you actually built what your CV claims | Be able to justify every architectural choice you made |
| Hiring manager | Ownership, conflict, how you handle being wrong | Six STAR stories including one genuine failure |

- **React Native/Flutter/Swift/Kotlin:** describe how react native/flutter/swift/kotlin fits into the systems you have built.
- **UI Design:** describe how ui design fits into the systems you have built.
- **State Management:** compare two approaches within state management and justify your default choice.
- **APIs:** walk through a trade-off you made using apis and what you would do differently.
- **App Store Deployment:** explain how you would debug a problem involving app store deployment in production.
- **Testing:** explain how you would debug a problem involving testing in production.
- **Performance:** walk through a trade-off you made using performance and what you would do differently.

## Career progression and where this path leads

| Stage | Typical years | Scope | Common next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Junior | 0–2 | Well-defined tasks, close review | Own a full feature without supervision |
| Mid-level | 3–5 | Features end to end, some mentoring | Own a service or subsystem |
| Senior | 6–9 | Systems, technical direction, cross-team work | Staff engineer or engineering manager |
| Lead / staff / manager | 10+ | Organisational leverage, architecture, hiring | Principal engineer, head of engineering, or founder |

Lateral moves are common and healthy from this role. Mobile App Developer experience transfers well into adjacent specialisations, product engineering, and technical leadership. Use [compare careers](https://www.skillta.tech/compare) to see how the salary, difficulty and demand of two paths stack up before committing.

## Mistakes that slow people down

1. Collecting tutorials instead of finishing projects. Completion is the skill being trained.
2. Learning adjacent tools before the core ones. Get React Native/Flutter/Swift/Kotlin and UI Design solid first.
3. Building only what the tutorial shows. The learning happens when something breaks and nobody has written the fix down.
4. Waiting until you feel ready to apply. Interview practice is a skill and it is trained by interviewing.
5. No public trail. A deployed link and a written case study is worth more than a private repository.
6. Ignoring fundamentals because the stack is modern. Complexity, data modelling and debugging are still what interviews test.

## Mobile App Developer — frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to become a mobile app developer?

8-12 months to job-ready for someone starting from scratch and studying 10–15 hours a week. People coming from an adjacent technical role usually move faster because they already understand how teams ship software.

### Is Mobile App Developer a good career in 2027?

Demand is rated high. Strong — mobile usage continues to grow. Cross-platform frameworks are making it easier to target both platforms.

### Do I need a degree to become a mobile app developer?

No, though it still helps for visa-sponsored roles and large enterprises. What replaces it is evidence: deployed projects, a public code history, and the ability to explain your decisions clearly.

### How hard is it really?

Difficulty is moderate — roughly 3 out of 10. Platform fragmentation is annoying. Dealing with app store reviews can be frustrating. But building something millions of people carry in their pocket is magical.

### What should I learn first?

Start with Fundamentals — specifically Choose Your Path, Programming Language and UI Basics. Everything later in the roadmap assumes this foundation.

### Can I switch to Mobile App Developer from a non-technical background?

Yes, and thousands do each year. The realistic timeline is 8-12 months (basics) → 2-3 years (expert), the main risk is quitting in month four, and the strongest mitigation is a public build streak plus one person who expects progress from you weekly.

### Will AI replace mobile app developers?

AI has changed the work rather than removed it. Code generation raised the floor, and the value moved toward design, debugging, evaluating correctness and understanding systems — the parts current models handle least reliably.

> **Next step:** Not certain this is your best fit? The [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) takes five minutes, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) to see exactly what stands between you and a mobile app developer role.

# Full-Stack Developer Roadmap

> Master both frontend and backend development

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/fullstack-developer

Full-stack developers handle everything — from pixel-perfect UIs to robust server architectures. You're the complete package every startup dreams of.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Hard |
| Time to job-ready | 12-18 months to job-ready |
| Demand | Very High |
| Salary (India) | ₹6-18 LPA (entry) → ₹20-50 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $65K-95K (entry) → $140K-230K+ (senior) |
| Growth | Outstanding — startups and mid-size companies heavily prefer full-stack developers for their versatility. |

## Required skills

- React/Next.js
- Node.js/Python
- Databases
- REST/GraphQL APIs
- DevOps Basics
- TypeScript
- System Design

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (2-3 months)

- **HTML/CSS/JS** — Web fundamentals and responsive design
- **Programming Logic** — Data structures, algorithms, OOP
- **Git & CLI** — Version control and command line proficiency

Resources:

- The Odin Project
- freeCodeCamp
- CS50

Projects:

- Personal website
- CLI tool
- Interactive form

### Phase 2: Frontend Mastery (2-3 months)

- **React & TypeScript** — Components, hooks, state management
- **Styling** — Tailwind CSS, responsive design, animations
- **API Consumption** — Fetching data, caching, error handling

Resources:

- React docs
- TypeScript Handbook
- Tailwind docs

Projects:

- Dashboard app
- E-commerce frontend
- Portfolio site

### Phase 3: Backend Mastery (2-3 months)

- **Node.js/Express** — Server-side logic, middleware, auth
- **Databases** — PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ORMs
- **Authentication** — JWT, OAuth, session management

Resources:

- Node.js docs
- Prisma docs
- MongoDB University

Projects:

- REST API
- Auth system
- Blog backend

### Phase 4: Full-Stack Projects (3-4 months)

- **Next.js** — SSR, API routes, full-stack framework
- **Deployment** — Vercel, Docker, CI/CD
- **Real-Time Features** — WebSockets, real-time updates

Resources:

- Next.js docs
- Vercel guides
- Socket.io

Projects:

- SaaS app
- Real-time chat
- Job board platform

### Phase 5: Job Preparation (1-2 months)

- **System Design** — Architecture decisions, trade-offs
- **DSA** — LeetCode medium problems
- **Portfolio** — 3-5 deployed full-stack projects

Resources:

- LeetCode
- System Design Primer
- Pramp

Projects:

- Polish GitHub
- Technical blog
- Mock interviews

## Reality check

Jack of all trades can mean master of none if you're not careful. Depth matters. But the career flexibility is unmatched — you can build anything.

## What a Full-Stack Developer actually does day to day

Full-stack developers handle everything — from pixel-perfect UIs to robust server architectures. You're the complete package every startup dreams of. In practice the week looks less like continuous coding and more like a mix of building, reviewing, debugging and deciding. A typical day includes a short stand-up, two to four hours of focused build time, code review for teammates, and at least one conversation about scope or trade-offs. The people who progress fastest in this role are the ones who treat those conversations as part of the job rather than as an interruption to it.

- **Morning:** triage anything that broke overnight, then take the highest-leverage task rather than the easiest one.
- **Core hours:** deep work on the current increment — React/Next.js, Node.js/Python and Databases are the tools you will touch most.
- **Reviews:** reading other people's changes is the fastest way to learn a codebase and the fastest way to build trust.
- **Documentation:** a short written note about why a decision was made saves hours for the next person, often you in three months.
- **Learning:** the field moves; an hour a week on fundamentals beats a weekend binge every quarter.

## Is Full-Stack Developer the right fit for you?

This path suits you if several of the following are true. It is worth being honest here — switching after six months costs far more than choosing carefully now.

- You want to build entire applications end-to-end
- You enjoy variety and switching between frontend and backend
- You thrive in startup environments
- You want maximum flexibility in your career

> **Honest difficulty:** Jack of all trades can mean master of none if you're not careful. Depth matters. But the career flexibility is unmatched — you can build anything. Competition is rated high and the entry barrier medium, with realistic time to job-ready around 12-18 months (basics) → 3-5 years (expert).

## Full-Stack Developer salary in 2027

Compensation for full-stack developers reflects scope more than years served. Outstanding — startups and mid-size companies heavily prefer full-stack developers for their versatility. The bands below are annual gross figures; product companies pay above them, services and agency employers below.

Full-Stack Developer salary bands, 2027

| Level | Experience | India | Global (USD) | What the role owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry / junior | 0–2 years | ₹6-18 LPA (entry) | $65K-95K (entry) | Well-scoped tasks with close review |
| Mid-level | 3–5 years | Between the entry and senior bands | Between the entry and senior bands | Owns features end to end, mentors juniors |
| Senior | 6+ years | ₹20-50 LPA (senior) | $140K-230K+ (senior) | Owns systems, sets technical direction |
| Lead / staff | 9+ years | Above the senior band, plus equity at product companies | Above the senior band, plus equity | Leverage through other engineers and architecture |

Three factors move you up these bands faster than time does: specialising in one high-demand area rather than staying general, owning a system end to end so you can describe impact in numbers, and changing employer at the right moment — external moves still outpace internal raises in most markets. Use the [salary predictor](https://www.skillta.tech/salary-predictor) to check the band for your specific city and experience level.

## The complete Full-Stack Developer skill map

You need 7 core competencies to be credible in interviews for this role. The table maps each one to why employers care and how it gets tested, so you can prioritise instead of trying to learn everything at once.

Core Full-Stack Developer skills and how they are assessed

| Skill | Why it matters | How interviewers test it | Time to proficiency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| React/Next.js | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |
| Node.js/Python | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Live coding exercise | 2–3 months |
| Databases | Most common source of production incidents when done badly | Debugging a broken example | 4–8 weeks |
| REST/GraphQL APIs | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |
| DevOps Basics | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Whiteboard or design discussion | 4–8 weeks |
| TypeScript | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Whiteboard or design discussion | 3–5 months |
| System Design | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 2–4 weeks |

| Weeks 13–14 | Phase 3: Backend Mastery | Node.js/Express — Server-side logic, middleware, auth | REST API |
| Weeks 15–16 | Phase 3: Backend Mastery | Databases — PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ORMs | Auth system |
| Weeks 17–18 | Phase 3: Backend Mastery | Authentication — JWT, OAuth, session management | Blog backend |
| Weeks 19–20 | Phase 4: Full-Stack Projects | Next.js — SSR, API routes, full-stack framework | SaaS app |
| Weeks 21–22 | Phase 4: Full-Stack Projects | Deployment — Vercel, Docker, CI/CD | Real-time chat |
| Weeks 23–24 | Phase 4: Full-Stack Projects | Real-Time Features — WebSockets, real-time updates | Job board platform |
| Weeks 25–26 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | System Design — Architecture decisions, trade-offs | Polish GitHub |
| Weeks 27–28 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | DSA — LeetCode medium problems | Technical blog |
| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Portfolio — 3-5 deployed full-stack projects | Mock interviews |

# Cloud Architect Roadmap

> Design and manage scalable cloud infrastructure

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/cloud-architect

Cloud architects design the infrastructure that powers modern applications. You decide how companies build, deploy, and scale their technology in the cloud.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Very Hard |
| Time to job-ready | 14-20 months to job-ready |
| Demand | Very High |
| Salary (India) | ₹10-25 LPA (entry) → ₹30-70 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $90K-130K (entry) → $160K-280K+ (senior) |
| Growth | Outstanding — cloud spending is growing 20%+ annually. Massive talent shortage. |

## Required skills

- AWS/Azure/GCP
- Networking
- Security
- Terraform/IaC
- Kubernetes
- Cost Optimization
- Architecture Patterns

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (2-3 months)

- **Networking** — TCP/IP, DNS, VPNs, load balancing
- **Linux** — System administration, scripting
- **Cloud Basics** — AWS/Azure core services overview

Resources:

- AWS Cloud Practitioner
- Linux Academy
- Cloud Computing Concepts

Projects:

- Set up VPC
- Deploy EC2 instances
- S3 static hosting

### Phase 2: Core Cloud Services (3-4 months)

- **Compute & Storage** — EC2, Lambda, S3, EBS, RDS
- **Networking & Security** — VPCs, IAM, security groups, WAF
- **Databases** — RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Aurora

Resources:

- AWS Solutions Architect prep
- A Cloud Guru
- Stephane Maarek courses

Projects:

- Multi-tier architecture
- Serverless API
- Database migration

### Phase 3: Advanced Architecture (3-4 months)

- **Infrastructure as Code** — Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi
- **Containers & Orchestration** — Docker, ECS, EKS, Kubernetes
- **CI/CD Pipelines** — CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

Resources:

- Terraform docs
- KodeKloud
- AWS Well-Architected

Projects:

- IaC full environment
- K8s cluster
- Blue-green deployment

### Phase 4: Specialization (2-3 months)

- **Cost Optimization** — Reserved instances, spot, rightsizing
- **Disaster Recovery** — Multi-region, backup strategies, RPO/RTO
- **Compliance** — HIPAA, SOC2, GDPR cloud compliance

Resources:

- AWS Cost Explorer
- Well-Architected Framework
- Cloud Security Alliance

Projects:

- Cost optimization audit
- DR plan implementation
- Compliance framework

### Phase 5: Certification & Job Prep (2-3 months)

- **AWS Solutions Architect Pro** — Professional-level certification
- **Architecture Portfolio** — Document architectures you've designed
- **Interview Prep** — Whiteboard architecture, case studies

Resources:

- AWS Certification
- Glassdoor
- LinkedIn

Projects:

- Architecture decision records
- Blog posts
- Mock design reviews

## Reality check

Requires years of hands-on experience. Most cloud architects start as DevOps or backend engineers first. The learning never stops as cloud services evolve constantly.

In practice the week looks less like continuous coding and more like a mix of building, reviewing, debugging and deciding. A typical day includes a short stand-up, two to four hours of focused build time, code review for teammates, and at least one conversation about scope or trade-offs. The people who progress fastest in this role are the ones who treat those conversations as part of the job rather than as an interruption to it.

- **Core hours:** deep work on the current increment — AWS/Azure/GCP, Networking and Security are the tools you will touch most.
- **Reviews:** reading other people's changes is the fastest way to learn a codebase and the fastest way to build trust.
- **Documentation:** a short written note about why a decision was made saves hours for the next person, often you in three months.
- **Learning:** the field moves; an hour a week on fundamentals beats a weekend binge every quarter.

- You love designing large-scale systems
- You enjoy optimizing for performance and cost
- You're fascinated by distributed computing
- You want one of the highest-paying tech roles

> **Honest difficulty:** Requires years of hands-on experience. Most cloud architects start as DevOps or backend engineers first. The learning never stops as cloud services evolve constantly. Competition is rated low and the entry barrier high, with realistic time to job-ready around 14-20 months (entry) → 4-6 years (expert).

| Weeks 1–2 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | Networking — TCP/IP, DNS, VPNs, load balancing | Set up VPC |
| Weeks 3–4 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | Linux — System administration, scripting | Deploy EC2 instances |
| Weeks 5–6 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | Cloud Basics — AWS/Azure core services overview | S3 static hosting |
| Weeks 7–8 | Phase 2: Core Cloud Services | Compute & Storage — EC2, Lambda, S3, EBS, RDS | Multi-tier architecture |
| Weeks 9–10 | Phase 2: Core Cloud Services | Networking & Security — VPCs, IAM, security groups, WAF | Serverless API |
| Weeks 11–12 | Phase 2: Core Cloud Services | Databases — RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Aurora | Database migration |
| Weeks 13–14 | Phase 3: Advanced Architecture | Infrastructure as Code — Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi | IaC full environment |
| Weeks 15–16 | Phase 3: Advanced Architecture | Containers & Orchestration — Docker, ECS, EKS, Kubernetes | K8s cluster |
| Weeks 17–18 | Phase 3: Advanced Architecture | CI/CD Pipelines — CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD | Blue-green deployment |
| Weeks 19–20 | Phase 4: Specialization | Cost Optimization — Reserved instances, spot, rightsizing | Cost optimization audit |
| Weeks 21–22 | Phase 4: Specialization | Disaster Recovery — Multi-region, backup strategies, RPO/RTO | DR plan implementation |
| Weeks 23–24 | Phase 4: Specialization | Compliance — HIPAA, SOC2, GDPR cloud compliance | Compliance framework |
| Weeks 25–26 | Phase 5: Certification & Job Prep | AWS Solutions Architect Pro — Professional-level certification | Architecture decision records |
| Weeks 27–28 | Phase 5: Certification & Job Prep | Architecture Portfolio — Document architectures you've designed | Blog posts |
| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Certification & Job Prep | Interview Prep — Whiteboard architecture, case studies | Mock design reviews |

## Portfolio projects that get interviews

Recruiters skim portfolios in under a minute, so two strong projects beat six weak ones. Each project below should be deployed, documented with a short README explaining the problem and the trade-offs, and something you can talk through for ten minutes without notes.

1. Set up VPC
2. Deploy EC2 instances
3. S3 static hosting
4. Multi-tier architecture
5. Serverless API
6. Database migration
7. IaC full environment
8. K8s cluster
9. Blue-green deployment
10. Cost optimization audit

Make at least one project unmistakably yours — solve a problem you actually have, use real data, and write up what broke. Interviewers ask far better questions about original work than about a cloned tutorial app, and those questions are the ones you will answer best.

## Free resources worth using

- AWS Cloud Practitioner
- Linux Academy
- Cloud Computing Concepts
- AWS Solutions Architect prep
- A Cloud Guru
- Stephane Maarek courses
- Terraform docs
- KodeKloud
- AWS Well-Architected
- AWS Cost Explorer
- Well-Architected Framework
- Cloud Security Alliance
- AWS Certification
- Glassdoor
- LinkedIn

Pick one primary resource and one reference. Rotating between five courses feels productive and teaches very little; finishing one and building alongside it teaches a lot. Official documentation should become your default reference within the first two months.

## Cloud Architect interview preparation

Interview loops for this role typically run four to six stages. Expect a recruiter screen, a technical screen on fundamentals, a practical exercise or take-home, a deep-dive on your own projects, and a hiring-manager conversation about ownership and collaboration.

| Round | What is tested | Preparation that works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Motivation, communication, salary alignment | A 90-second summary of your work and a researched range |
| Technical fundamentals | AWS/Azure/GCP, Networking and Security | Daily reps for four weeks, explained out loud |
| Practical exercise | Code quality, tests, judgement about scope | Timebox it and document what you deliberately left out |
| Project deep-dive | Whether you actually built what your CV claims | Be able to justify every architectural choice you made |
| Hiring manager | Ownership, conflict, how you handle being wrong | Six STAR stories including one genuine failure |

- **Networking:** walk through a trade-off you made using networking and what you would do differently.
- **Security:** explain how you would debug a problem involving security in production.
- **Terraform/IaC:** compare two approaches within terraform/iac and justify your default choice.
- **Kubernetes:** explain how you would debug a problem involving kubernetes in production.
- **Cost Optimization:** compare two approaches within cost optimization and justify your default choice.
- **Architecture Patterns:** explain how you would debug a problem involving architecture patterns in production.
- **AWS/Azure/GCP:** compare two approaches within aws/azure/gcp and justify your default choice.

## Career progression and where this path leads

| Stage | Typical years | Scope | Common next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Junior | 0–2 | Well-defined tasks, close review | Own a full feature without supervision |
| Mid-level | 3–5 | Features end to end, some mentoring | Own a service or subsystem |
| Senior | 6–9 | Systems, technical direction, cross-team work | Staff engineer or engineering manager |
| Lead / staff / manager | 10+ | Organisational leverage, architecture, hiring | Principal engineer, head of engineering, or founder |

Lateral moves are common and healthy from this role. Cloud Architect experience transfers well into adjacent specialisations, product engineering, and technical leadership. Use [compare careers](https://www.skillta.tech/compare) to see how the salary, difficulty and demand of two paths stack up before committing.

## Mistakes that slow people down

1. Collecting tutorials instead of finishing projects. Completion is the skill being trained.
2. Learning adjacent tools before the core ones. Get AWS/Azure/GCP and Networking solid first.
3. Building only what the tutorial shows. The learning happens when something breaks and nobody has written the fix down.
4. Waiting until you feel ready to apply. Interview practice is a skill and it is trained by interviewing.
5. No public trail. A deployed link and a written case study is worth more than a private repository.
6. Ignoring fundamentals because the stack is modern. Complexity, data modelling and debugging are still what interviews test.

## Cloud Architect — frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to become a cloud architect?

14-20 months to job-ready for someone starting from scratch and studying 20+ hours a week. People coming from an adjacent technical role usually move faster because they already understand how teams ship software.

### Is Cloud Architect a good career in 2027?

Demand is rated very high. Outstanding — cloud spending is growing 20%+ annually. Massive talent shortage.

### Do I need a degree to become a cloud architect?

No, though it still helps for visa-sponsored roles and large enterprises. What replaces it is evidence: deployed projects, a public code history, and the ability to explain your decisions clearly.

### How hard is it really?

Difficulty is very hard — roughly 5 out of 10. Requires years of hands-on experience. Most cloud architects start as DevOps or backend engineers first. The learning never stops as cloud services evolve constantly.

### What should I learn first?

Start with Fundamentals — specifically Networking, Linux and Cloud Basics. Everything later in the roadmap assumes this foundation.

### Can I switch to Cloud Architect from a non-technical background?

Yes, and thousands do each year. The realistic timeline is 14-20 months (entry) → 4-6 years (expert), the main risk is quitting in month four, and the strongest mitigation is a public build streak plus one person who expects progress from you weekly.

### Will AI replace cloud architects?

AI has changed the work rather than removed it. Code generation raised the floor, and the value moved toward design, debugging, evaluating correctness and understanding systems — the parts current models handle least reliably.

> **Next step:** Not certain this is your best fit? The [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) takes five minutes, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) to see exactly what stands between you and a cloud architect role.

- [Blog](https://www.skillta.tech/blog)

# AI/ML Engineer Roadmap

> Build intelligent systems that learn and adapt

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/ai-ml-engineer

AI/ML engineers build and deploy machine learning models that power intelligent features — from recommendation systems to computer vision and NLP.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Very Hard |
| Time to job-ready | 14-20 months to job-ready |
| Demand | Very High |
| Salary (India) | ₹8-22 LPA (entry) → ₹30-70 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $80K-120K (entry) → $160K-300K+ (senior) |
| Growth | Explosive — AI is transforming every industry. Demand far exceeds supply. |

## Required skills

- Python
- TensorFlow/PyTorch
- Mathematics
- Deep Learning
- MLOps
- Data Engineering
- Cloud ML Services

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (2-3 months)

- **Python Mastery** — Advanced Python, OOP, data structures
- **Mathematics** — Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics
- **Data Handling** — Pandas, NumPy, data preprocessing

Resources:

- 3Blue1Brown
- Khan Academy
- Python for Data Science

Projects:

- Data analysis pipeline
- Statistical visualizations
- Math implementation library

### Phase 2: Machine Learning (3-4 months)

- **Classical ML** — Regression, classification, clustering, ensemble methods
- **Feature Engineering** — Feature selection, extraction, transformation
- **Model Evaluation** — Cross-validation, metrics, hyperparameter tuning

Resources:

- Andrew Ng ML Course
- Scikit-learn docs
- Kaggle

Projects:

- Prediction models
- Kaggle competition
- ML pipeline

### Phase 3: Deep Learning (3-4 months)

- **Neural Networks** — CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, GANs
- **NLP** — Text classification, sentiment analysis, LLMs
- **Computer Vision** — Image classification, object detection, segmentation

Resources:

- fast.ai
- Deep Learning Specialization
- Hugging Face

Projects:

- Image classifier
- Chatbot
- Object detection system

### Phase 4: MLOps & Deployment (2-3 months)

- **Model Deployment** — Flask/FastAPI, Docker, model serving
- **MLOps** — MLflow, experiment tracking, model monitoring
- **Cloud ML** — AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Azure ML

Resources:

- MLOps Zoomcamp
- AWS ML docs
- Made With ML

Projects:

- End-to-end ML pipeline
- Model monitoring dashboard
- A/B testing framework

### Phase 5: Job Preparation (1-2 months)

- **Research Papers** — Read and implement key papers
- **Portfolio** — GitHub repos, blog posts, Kaggle profile
- **Interviews** — ML theory, coding, system design

Resources:

- Papers With Code
- Kaggle
- Interview resources

Projects:

- Paper implementation
- End-to-end ML project
- Technical blog

## Reality check

The hype is real but so is the math. Many 'AI engineers' are actually data pipeline builders. True ML work requires deep mathematical understanding. But the field is genuinely transformative.

## What a AI/ML Engineer actually does day to day

AI/ML engineers build and deploy machine learning models that power intelligent features — from recommendation systems to computer vision and NLP. In practice the week looks less like continuous coding and more like a mix of building, reviewing, debugging and deciding. A typical day includes a short stand-up, two to four hours of focused build time, code review for teammates, and at least one conversation about scope or trade-offs. The people who progress fastest in this role are the ones who treat those conversations as part of the job rather than as an interruption to it.

- **Morning:** triage anything that broke overnight, then take the highest-leverage task rather than the easiest one.
- **Core hours:** deep work on the current increment — Python, TensorFlow/PyTorch and Mathematics are the tools you will touch most.
- **Reviews:** reading other people's changes is the fastest way to learn a codebase and the fastest way to build trust.
- **Documentation:** a short written note about why a decision was made saves hours for the next person, often you in three months.
- **Learning:** the field moves; an hour a week on fundamentals beats a weekend binge every quarter.

## Is AI/ML Engineer the right fit for you?

This path suits you if several of the following are true. It is worth being honest here — switching after six months costs far more than choosing carefully now.

- You're passionate about artificial intelligence
- You have strong math and programming skills
- You want to work on cutting-edge technology
- You enjoy research and experimentation

> **Honest difficulty:** The hype is real but so is the math. Many 'AI engineers' are actually data pipeline builders. True ML work requires deep mathematical understanding. But the field is genuinely transformative. Competition is rated high and the entry barrier high, with realistic time to job-ready around 14-20 months (basics) → 4-6 years (expert).

## AI/ML Engineer salary in 2027

Compensation for ai/ml engineers reflects scope more than years served. Explosive — AI is transforming every industry. Demand far exceeds supply. The bands below are annual gross figures; product companies pay above them, services and agency employers below.

AI/ML Engineer salary bands, 2027

| Level | Experience | India | Global (USD) | What the role owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry / junior | 0–2 years | ₹8-22 LPA (entry) | $80K-120K (entry) | Well-scoped tasks with close review |
| Mid-level | 3–5 years | Between the entry and senior bands | Between the entry and senior bands | Owns features end to end, mentors juniors |
| Senior | 6+ years | ₹30-70 LPA (senior) | $160K-300K+ (senior) | Owns systems, sets technical direction |
| Lead / staff | 9+ years | Above the senior band, plus equity at product companies | Above the senior band, plus equity | Leverage through other engineers and architecture |

Three factors move you up these bands faster than time does: specialising in one high-demand area rather than staying general, owning a system end to end so you can describe impact in numbers, and changing employer at the right moment — external moves still outpace internal raises in most markets. Use the [salary predictor](https://www.skillta.tech/salary-predictor) to check the band for your specific city and experience level.

## The complete AI/ML Engineer skill map

You need 7 core competencies to be credible in interviews for this role. The table maps each one to why employers care and how it gets tested, so you can prioritise instead of trying to learn everything at once.

Core AI/ML Engineer skills and how they are assessed

| Skill | Why it matters | How interviewers test it | Time to proficiency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Deep questions about a project on your CV | 3–5 months |
| TensorFlow/PyTorch | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Debugging a broken example | 4–8 weeks |
| Mathematics | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Debugging a broken example | 4–8 weeks |
| Deep Learning | Most common source of production incidents when done badly | Debugging a broken example | 2–3 months |
| MLOps | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Whiteboard or design discussion | 2–4 weeks |
| Data Engineering | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |
| Cloud ML Services | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 4–8 weeks |

| Weeks 15–16 | Phase 3: Deep Learning | NLP — Text classification, sentiment analysis, LLMs | Chatbot |
| Weeks 17–18 | Phase 3: Deep Learning | Computer Vision — Image classification, object detection, segmentation | Object detection system |
| Weeks 19–20 | Phase 4: MLOps & Deployment | Model Deployment — Flask/FastAPI, Docker, model serving | End-to-end ML pipeline |
| Weeks 21–22 | Phase 4: MLOps & Deployment | MLOps — MLflow, experiment tracking, model monitoring | Model monitoring dashboard |
| Weeks 23–24 | Phase 4: MLOps & Deployment | Cloud ML — AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Azure ML | A/B testing framework |

| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Interviews — ML theory, coding, system design | Technical blog |

# Blockchain Developer Roadmap

> Build decentralized applications and smart contracts

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/roadmaps/blockchain-developer

Blockchain developers create decentralized applications, smart contracts, and Web3 solutions that power the next generation of trustless, transparent systems.

## Key facts

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Difficulty | Hard |
| Time to job-ready | 10-16 months to job-ready |
| Demand | Growing |
| Salary (India) | ₹6-18 LPA (entry) → ₹25-60 LPA (senior) |
| Salary (Global) | $70K-110K (entry) → $150K-300K+ (senior) |
| Growth | High but volatile — the space goes through cycles. Skilled blockchain devs are always in demand. |

## Required skills

- Solidity/Rust
- Ethereum/Solana
- Smart Contracts
- Web3.js/Ethers.js
- DeFi Protocols
- Security Auditing
- Cryptography

## Learning roadmap

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (2-3 months)

- **Blockchain Concepts** — Consensus mechanisms, hashing, distributed ledgers
- **JavaScript/TypeScript** — Strong programming foundation
- **Cryptography Basics** — Public-key cryptography, hashing, digital signatures

Resources:

- Bitcoin Whitepaper
- Mastering Ethereum
- CryptoZombies

Projects:

- Simple blockchain in JS
- Hash function implementation
- Wallet generator

### Phase 2: Smart Contracts (3-4 months)

- **Solidity** — Language fundamentals, patterns, best practices
- **Hardhat/Foundry** — Development environment, testing, deployment
- **ERC Standards** — ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155 tokens

Resources:

- Solidity docs
- Patrick Collins courses
- OpenZeppelin

Projects:

- ERC-20 token
- NFT collection
- Simple DEX

### Phase 3: DApp Development (2-3 months)

- **Web3.js/Ethers.js** — Blockchain interaction from frontend
- **Frontend Integration** — React + wallet connection, transaction UX
- **IPFS & Storage** — Decentralized storage solutions

Resources:

- Ethers.js docs
- Alchemy University
- IPFS docs

Projects:

- Full DApp
- NFT marketplace
- DAO voting system

### Phase 4: Advanced Topics (2-3 months)

- **Security Auditing** — Common vulnerabilities, reentrancy, overflow
- **DeFi Protocols** — AMMs, lending, yield farming mechanics
- **L2 Solutions** — Rollups, sidechains, scaling solutions

Resources:

- Damn Vulnerable DeFi
- Secureum
- L2Beat

Projects:

- Security audit report
- DeFi protocol clone
- Cross-chain bridge concept

### Phase 5: Job Preparation (1-2 months)

- **Portfolio** — Deployed contracts, audited projects
- **Open Source** — Contribute to Web3 libraries
- **Networking** — Web3 communities, hackathons

Resources:

- ETHGlobal
- Gitcoin
- Web3 job boards

Projects:

- Hackathon participation
- Security audit practice
- Technical blog

The space is volatile and full of hype. Many projects are scams. But the core technology is genuinely innovative, and the developer community is passionate and rewarding.

## What a Blockchain Developer actually does day to day

Blockchain developers create decentralized applications, smart contracts, and Web3 solutions that power the next generation of trustless, transparent systems. In practice the week looks less like continuous coding and more like a mix of building, reviewing, debugging and deciding. A typical day includes a short stand-up, two to four hours of focused build time, code review for teammates, and at least one conversation about scope or trade-offs. The people who progress fastest in this role are the ones who treat those conversations as part of the job rather than as an interruption to it.

- **Core hours:** deep work on the current increment — Solidity/Rust, Ethereum/Solana and Smart Contracts are the tools you will touch most.
- **Reviews:** reading other people's changes is the fastest way to learn a codebase and the fastest way to build trust.

- You're fascinated by decentralization and cryptography

- You enjoy both backend and financial systems
- You believe in building trustless systems

> **Honest difficulty:** The space is volatile and full of hype. Many projects are scams. But the core technology is genuinely innovative, and the developer community is passionate and rewarding. ## The complete Blockchain Developer skill map

You need 7 core competencies to be credible in interviews for this role. The table maps each one to why employers care and how it gets tested, so you can prioritise instead of trying to learn everything at once.

Core Blockchain Developer skills and how they are assessed

| Skill | Why it matters | How interviewers test it | Time to proficiency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Solidity/Rust | Most common source of production incidents when done badly | Live coding exercise | 2–4 weeks |
| Ethereum/Solana | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 4–8 weeks |
| Smart Contracts | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Debugging a broken example | 2–4 weeks |
| Web3.js/Ethers.js | The difference between shipping and shipping something maintainable | Whiteboard or design discussion | 2–4 weeks |
| DeFi Protocols | Foundation that every later topic depends on | Live coding exercise | 3–5 months |
| Security Auditing | What separates a mid-level candidate from a junior one | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 2–3 months |
| Cryptography | Most common source of production incidents when done badly | Take-home review and follow-up questions | 2–3 months |

## Week-by-week Blockchain Developer learning plan

The roadmap phases above tell you what to learn. This plan tells you when, assuming 15–20 hours a week of focused study. Slipping a week is normal; skipping the build column is not — the projects are what make the learning stick and what fills your portfolio.

Week-by-week Blockchain Developer study plan (15–20 hours a week)

| Timeline | Phase | What to learn | What to build that week |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weeks 1–2 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | Blockchain Concepts — Consensus mechanisms, hashing, distributed ledgers | Simple blockchain in JS |
| Weeks 3–4 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | JavaScript/TypeScript — Strong programming foundation | Hash function implementation |
| Weeks 5–6 | Phase 1: Fundamentals | Cryptography Basics — Public-key cryptography, hashing, digital signatures | Wallet generator |
| Weeks 7–8 | Phase 2: Smart Contracts | Solidity — Language fundamentals, patterns, best practices | ERC-20 token |
| Weeks 9–10 | Phase 2: Smart Contracts | Hardhat/Foundry — Development environment, testing, deployment | NFT collection |
| Weeks 11–12 | Phase 2: Smart Contracts | ERC Standards — ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155 tokens | Simple DEX |
| Weeks 13–14 | Phase 3: DApp Development | Web3.js/Ethers.js — Blockchain interaction from frontend | Full DApp |
| Weeks 15–16 | Phase 3: DApp Development | Frontend Integration — React + wallet connection, transaction UX | NFT marketplace |
| Weeks 17–18 | Phase 3: DApp Development | IPFS & Storage — Decentralized storage solutions | DAO voting system |
| Weeks 19–20 | Phase 4: Advanced Topics | Security Auditing — Common vulnerabilities, reentrancy, overflow | Security audit report |
| Weeks 21–22 | Phase 4: Advanced Topics | DeFi Protocols — AMMs, lending, yield farming mechanics | DeFi protocol clone |
| Weeks 23–24 | Phase 4: Advanced Topics | L2 Solutions — Rollups, sidechains, scaling solutions | Cross-chain bridge concept |
| Weeks 25–26 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Portfolio — Deployed contracts, audited projects | Hackathon participation |
| Weeks 27–28 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Open Source — Contribute to Web3 libraries | Security audit practice |
| Weeks 29–30 | Phase 5: Job Preparation | Networking — Web3 communities, hackathons | Technical blog |

## Portfolio projects that get interviews

Recruiters skim portfolios in under a minute, so two strong projects beat six weak ones. Each project below should be deployed, documented with a short README explaining the problem and the trade-offs, and something you can talk through for ten minutes without notes.

1. Simple blockchain in JS
2. Hash function implementation
3. Wallet generator
4. ERC-20 token
5. NFT collection
6. Simple DEX
7. Full DApp
8. NFT marketplace
9. DAO voting system
10. Security audit report

Make at least one project unmistakably yours — solve a problem you actually have, use real data, and write up what broke. Interviewers ask far better questions about original work than about a cloned tutorial app, and those questions are the ones you will answer best.

## Free resources worth using

- Bitcoin Whitepaper
- Mastering Ethereum
- CryptoZombies
- Solidity docs
- Patrick Collins courses
- OpenZeppelin
- Ethers.js docs
- Alchemy University
- IPFS docs
- Damn Vulnerable DeFi
- Secureum
- L2Beat
- ETHGlobal
- Gitcoin
- Web3 job boards

Pick one primary resource and one reference. Rotating between five courses feels productive and teaches very little; finishing one and building alongside it teaches a lot. Official documentation should become your default reference within the first two months.

## Blockchain Developer interview preparation

Interview loops for this role typically run four to six stages. Expect a recruiter screen, a technical screen on fundamentals, a practical exercise or take-home, a deep-dive on your own projects, and a hiring-manager conversation about ownership and collaboration.

| Round | What is tested | Preparation that works |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Motivation, communication, salary alignment | A 90-second summary of your work and a researched range |
| Technical fundamentals | Solidity/Rust, Ethereum/Solana and Smart Contracts | Daily reps for four weeks, explained out loud |
| Practical exercise | Code quality, tests, judgement about scope | Timebox it and document what you deliberately left out |
| Project deep-dive | Whether you actually built what your CV claims | Be able to justify every architectural choice you made |
| Hiring manager | Ownership, conflict, how you handle being wrong | Six STAR stories including one genuine failure |

- **Cryptography:** compare two approaches within cryptography and justify your default choice.
- **Solidity/Rust:** explain how you would debug a problem involving solidity/rust in production.
- **Ethereum/Solana:** compare two approaches within ethereum/solana and justify your default choice.
- **Smart Contracts:** describe how smart contracts fits into the systems you have built.
- **Web3.js/Ethers.js:** describe how web3.js/ethers.js fits into the systems you have built.
- **DeFi Protocols:** walk through a trade-off you made using defi protocols and what you would do differently.
- **Security Auditing:** describe how security auditing fits into the systems you have built.

## Career progression and where this path leads

| Stage | Typical years | Scope | Common next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Junior | 0–2 | Well-defined tasks, close review | Own a full feature without supervision |
| Mid-level | 3–5 | Features end to end, some mentoring | Own a service or subsystem |
| Senior | 6–9 | Systems, technical direction, cross-team work | Staff engineer or engineering manager |
| Lead / staff / manager | 10+ | Organisational leverage, architecture, hiring | Principal engineer, head of engineering, or founder |

Lateral moves are common and healthy from this role. Blockchain Developer experience transfers well into adjacent specialisations, product engineering, and technical leadership. Use [compare careers](https://www.skillta.tech/compare) to see how the salary, difficulty and demand of two paths stack up before committing.

## Mistakes that slow people down

1. Collecting tutorials instead of finishing projects. Completion is the skill being trained.
2. Learning adjacent tools before the core ones. Get Solidity/Rust and Ethereum/Solana solid first.
3. Building only what the tutorial shows. The learning happens when something breaks and nobody has written the fix down.
4. Waiting until you feel ready to apply. Interview practice is a skill and it is trained by interviewing.
5. No public trail. A deployed link and a written case study is worth more than a private repository.
6. Ignoring fundamentals because the stack is modern. Complexity, data modelling and debugging are still what interviews test.

## Blockchain Developer — frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to become a blockchain developer?

10-16 months to job-ready for someone starting from scratch and studying 15–20 hours a week. People coming from an adjacent technical role usually move faster because they already understand how teams ship software.

### Is Blockchain Developer a good career in 2027?

Demand is rated growing. High but volatile — the space goes through cycles. Skilled blockchain devs are always in demand.

### Do I need a degree to become a blockchain developer?

No, though it still helps for visa-sponsored roles and large enterprises. What replaces it is evidence: deployed projects, a public code history, and the ability to explain your decisions clearly.

### How hard is it really?

Difficulty is hard — roughly 4 out of 10. The space is volatile and full of hype. Many projects are scams. But the core technology is genuinely innovative, and the developer community is passionate and rewarding.

### What should I learn first?

Start with Fundamentals — specifically Blockchain Concepts, JavaScript/TypeScript and Cryptography Basics. Everything later in the roadmap assumes this foundation.

### Can I switch to Blockchain Developer from a non-technical background?

Yes, and thousands do each year. The realistic timeline is 10-16 months (entry) → 3-5 years (expert), the main risk is quitting in month four, and the strongest mitigation is a public build streak plus one person who expects progress from you weekly.

### Will AI replace blockchain developers?

AI has changed the work rather than removed it. Code generation raised the floor, and the value moved toward design, debugging, evaluating correctness and understanding systems — the parts current models handle least reliably.

# Software Engineer Salary in USA (2027): Entry-Level, Senior & Lead Pay — FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights

> Complete 2027 Software Engineer salary breakdown for USA: entry $110K USD, mid $165K USD, senior $235K USD. City-wise pay, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, top employers & premium skills covered.

Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## Software Engineer Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Software Engineer** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Software Engineer in USA in 2027 sits around **$165K USD/year**. Entry $110K. Senior $235K. Staff/Lead $340K.

## What a Software Engineer Actually Does

- Design and implement production services (usually REST/gRPC APIs)
- Own code quality: reviews, tests, CI, observability
- Debug production incidents and contribute to postmortems
- Collaborate with PM/design to break epics into shippable slices

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Software Engineer Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (USD) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | $110K |
| Mid | 2–5 | $165K |
| Senior | 5–8 | $235K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | $340K |

Figures are total compensation (base + bonus + equity vest) pre-tax. Effective federal + state tax averages 28–37% depending on state.

## City-wise Software Engineer Salary in USA

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|

| New York City | $132K | $198K | $282K |

| Austin | $112K | $168K | $240K |
| Denver | $105K | $157K | $223K |
| Atlanta | $99K | $149K | $212K |

- **Meta**
- **Amazon**
- **Microsoft**
- **Apple**
- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Distributed systems (Kafka, Kubernetes)
- Go or Rust for infra roles
- LLM integration (RAG, function calling)
- Security-first coding (OWASP, threat modeling)
- System design at scale

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **SWE I (0–2 yr)**
2. **SWE II (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior SWE (4–7 yr)**
4. **Staff SWE (7–10 yr)**
5. **Principal / Distinguished (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Software Engineer Salary in USA

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## Why software engineer salary usa matters in 2027

Complete 2027 Software Engineer salary breakdown for USA: entry $110K USD, mid $165K USD, senior $235K USD. City-wise pay, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, top employers & premium skills covered. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · usa right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for software engineer salary usa filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is software engineer salary usa still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

## Why qa engineer salary usa matters in 2027

QA Engineer pay in USA for 2027 — mid-level $112K USD, senior tops $158K USD. See FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, hiring companies and skills that unlock a 30% raise. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · usa right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for qa engineer salary usa filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is qa engineer salary usa still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

### What should I do first?

Take the [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) if you are still choosing a direction, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) if you already have a target role and need to know what to learn next.

- [Compare two careers side by side](https://www.skillta.tech/compare) — salary, difficulty, demand and growth in one view.
