# How Much Does a Data Scientist Earn in USA? 2027 Report (FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights)

> How much does a Data Scientist really make in USA in 2027? Full report with FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, entry $118K USD to lead $335K USD bands, bonuses & equity insights.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/data-scientist-salary-in-usa-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## Data Scientist Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Data Scientist** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Data Scientist in USA in 2027 sits around **$168K USD/year**. Entry $118K. Senior $240K. Staff/Lead $335K.

## What a Data Scientist Actually Does

- Frame business questions into modeling problems
- Build and validate models (regression, tree ensembles, embeddings)
- Run A/B tests and causal analyses
- Communicate findings to non-technical stakeholders

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Data Scientist Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (USD) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | $118K |
| Mid | 2–5 | $168K |
| Senior | 5–8 | $240K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | $335K |

Figures are total compensation (base + bonus + equity vest) pre-tax. Effective federal + state tax averages 28–37% depending on state.

## City-wise Data Scientist Salary in USA

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| San Francisco Bay Area | $159K | $227K | $324K |
| New York City | $142K | $202K | $288K |
| Seattle | $139K | $198K | $283K |
| Boston | $127K | $181K | $259K |
| Austin | $120K | $171K | $245K |
| Denver | $112K | $160K | $228K |
| Atlanta | $106K | $151K | $216K |

## Top Companies Hiring Data Scientists in USA (2027)

- **Google**
- **Meta**
- **Amazon**
- **Microsoft**
- **Apple**
- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**
- **Anthropic**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Causal inference & experimentation
- Deep learning (PyTorch)
- LLM fine-tuning & evals
- Databricks / Snowflake at scale
- MLOps (MLflow, Airflow, dbt)

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Junior DS (0–2 yr)**
2. **Data Scientist (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior DS (4–7 yr)**
4. **Principal DS / Applied Scientist (7–10 yr)**
5. **Head of DS (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Data Scientist Salary in USA

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

**How long does it take to reach senior Data Scientist in USA?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

# DevOps Engineer Jobs in USA 2027: Average Salary, FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights & Top Employers

> DevOps Engineer jobs in USA pay around $162K USD mid-level in 2027. Explore FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, top hiring firms, remote rates and negotiation tactics.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/devops-engineer-salary-in-usa-2026

## DevOps Engineer Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

- Design and operate CI/CD pipelines
- Run Kubernetes clusters, service mesh, observability stack
- Own IaC (Terraform, Pulumi) and cloud cost
- Lead incident response and SLO/error-budget practice

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is devops engineer salary usa still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

# AI/ML Engineer Salary Guide — USA 2027: Bands, Bonuses, Equity & FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights

> 2027 AI/ML Engineer salary guide for USA: bands from $138K USD to $420K USD, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, in-demand skills and how to climb the career ladder faster.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/ai-ml-engineer-salary-in-usa-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## AI/ML Engineer Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **AI/ML Engineer** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level AI/ML Engineer in USA in 2027 sits around **$195K USD/year**. Entry $138K. Senior $285K. Staff/Lead $420K.

## What a AI/ML Engineer Actually Does

- Train, fine-tune, and evaluate ML/LLM models
- Ship model serving infra (Triton, vLLM, Ray Serve)
- Build RAG, agentic, and multimodal pipelines
- Own model quality: evals, hallucination guardrails, drift monitoring

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## AI/ML Engineer Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (USD) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | $138K |
| Mid | 2–5 | $195K |
| Senior | 5–8 | $285K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | $420K |

Figures are total compensation (base + bonus + equity vest) pre-tax. Effective federal + state tax averages 28–37% depending on state.

## City-wise AI/ML Engineer Salary in USA

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| San Francisco Bay Area | $186K | $263K | $385K |
| New York City | $166K | $234K | $342K |
| Seattle | $163K | $230K | $336K |
| Boston | $149K | $211K | $308K |
| Austin | $141K | $199K | $291K |
| Denver | $131K | $185K | $271K |
| Atlanta | $124K | $176K | $257K |

## Top Companies Hiring AI/ML Engineers in USA (2027)

- **Google**
- **Meta**
- **Amazon**
- **Microsoft**
- **Apple**
- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**
- **Anthropic**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- LLM fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA)
- vLLM / TensorRT-LLM inference
- Vector DBs (Qdrant, pgvector, Weaviate)
- LangGraph / agentic orchestration
- GPU cost & performance tuning

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **ML Engineer I (0–2 yr)**
2. **ML Engineer II (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior MLE (4–7 yr)**
4. **Staff MLE / Research Engineer (7–10 yr)**
5. **Principal (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your AI/ML Engineer Salary in USA

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## FAQ

**Is AI/ML Engineer still a good career in USA in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for AI/ML Engineers in USA is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

**How long does it take to reach senior AI/ML Engineer in USA?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

**Does remote work pay the same as on-site in USA?**
Usually within 5–15% of the metro band. Fully-remote roles from US-HQ employers often pay above local averages for non-US countries.

*Data compiled early 2027 from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow Dev Survey 2025, and LinkedIn Talent Insights. Individual offers vary; use this as a negotiation baseline, not a guarantee.*


## Why ai/ml engineer salary usa matters in 2027

2027 AI/ML Engineer salary guide for USA: bands from $138K USD to $420K USD, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, in-demand skills and how to climb the career ladder faster. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · usa right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for ai/ml engineer salary usa filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

# Cloud Architect Pay in USA (2027): FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights and the Full Career-Ladder Breakdown

> Cloud Architect pay in USA (2027): $200K USD mid, $280K USD senior. Career ladder, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers and premium skills that command 20–35% higher offers.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/cloud-architect-salary-in-usa-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## Cloud Architect Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Cloud Architect** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Cloud Architect in USA in 2027 sits around **$200K USD/year**. Entry $145K. Senior $280K. Staff/Lead $380K.

## What a Cloud Architect Actually Does

- Design cloud landing zones and multi-account strategy
- Set standards for IAM, networking, and data residency
- Model cost and drive FinOps guardrails
- Partner with security & compliance on control frameworks

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Cloud Architect Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (USD) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | $145K |
| Mid | 2–5 | $200K |
| Senior | 5–8 | $280K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | $380K |

Figures are total compensation (base + bonus + equity vest) pre-tax. Effective federal + state tax averages 28–37% depending on state.

## City-wise Cloud Architect Salary in USA

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| San Francisco Bay Area | $196K | $270K | $378K |
| New York City | $174K | $240K | $336K |
| Seattle | $171K | $236K | $330K |
| Boston | $157K | $216K | $302K |
| Austin | $148K | $204K | $286K |
| Denver | $138K | $190K | $266K |
| Atlanta | $131K | $180K | $252K |

## Top Companies Hiring Cloud Architects in USA (2027)

- **Google**
- **Meta**
- **Amazon**
- **Microsoft**
- **Apple**
- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**
- **Anthropic**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Multi-cloud (AWS + GCP + Azure)
- Kubernetes + service mesh design
- Zero-trust networking
- FinOps & unit economics
- Data mesh / lakehouse design

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Cloud Engineer (0–3 yr)**
2. **Cloud Architect I (3–6 yr)**
3. **Senior Architect (6–9 yr)**
4. **Principal Architect (9–12 yr)**
5. **Distinguished / Chief Architect (12+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Cloud Architect Salary in USA

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## FAQ

**Is Cloud Architect still a good career in USA in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for Cloud Architects in USA is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

**How long does it take to reach senior Cloud Architect in USA?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

**Does remote work pay the same as on-site in USA?**
Usually within 5–15% of the metro band. Fully-remote roles from US-HQ employers often pay above local averages for non-US countries.

*Data compiled early 2027 from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow Dev Survey 2025, and LinkedIn Talent Insights. Individual offers vary; use this as a negotiation baseline, not a guarantee.*


## Why cloud architect salary usa matters in 2027

Cloud Architect pay in USA (2027): $200K USD mid, $280K USD senior. Career ladder, FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers and premium skills that command 20–35% higher offers. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · usa right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for cloud architect salary usa filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is cloud architect salary usa still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

# Is Technical Product Manager Worth It in USA in 2027? Salary Data, Demand & FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights

> Should you pursue Technical Product Manager in USA in 2027? Latest salary bands ($135K USD–$360K USD), demand trends and FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers — all in one guide.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/product-manager-salary-in-usa-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## Technical Product Manager Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Technical Product Manager** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Technical Product Manager in USA in 2027 sits around **$185K USD/year**. Entry $135K. Senior $265K. Staff/Lead $360K.

## What a Technical Product Manager Actually Does

- Own product strategy for a technical surface (API, platform, ML)
- Write PRDs, run discovery, prioritize the backlog
- Partner with engineering on architecture trade-offs
- Drive metrics: activation, retention, revenue, model quality

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Technical Product Manager Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**
- **Anthropic**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- AI/LLM product sense
- Data literacy (SQL, dashboards)
- Experimentation & causal thinking
- Developer platforms / API PM
- Enterprise / SaaS pricing

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Associate PM (0–2 yr)**
2. **Product Manager (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior PM (4–7 yr)**
4. **Group / Principal PM (7–10 yr)**
5. **Director / VP Product (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Technical Product Manager Salary in USA

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## FAQ

**Is Technical Product Manager still a good career in USA in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for Technical Product Managers in USA is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

## Why technical product manager salary usa matters in 2027

Should you pursue Technical Product Manager in USA in 2027? Latest salary bands ($135K USD–$360K USD), demand trends and FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers — all in one guide. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · usa right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for technical product manager salary usa filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is technical product manager salary usa still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

### What should I do first?

Take the [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) if you are still choosing a direction, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) if you already have a target role and need to know what to learn next.

# Full Stack Developer Salary in USA 2027 — FAANG, State-Wise Pay & H1B Insights, Remote Rates & Contractor Pay

> Full Stack Developer salary in USA 2027 — full data on FAANG bands, state-wise pay (California, Texas, NY) and H1B-friendly employers, remote pay, contractor rates and the skills separating mid from senior offers.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/fullstack-developer-salary-in-usa-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · USA


## Full Stack Developer Salary in USA 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Full Stack Developer** role in USA in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Full Stack Developer in USA in 2027 sits around **$142K USD/year**. Entry $98K. Senior $200K. Staff/Lead $275K.

## What a Full Stack Developer Actually Does

- Own features end-to-end: UI, API, DB, deploy
- Ship on modern stacks (Next.js + tRPC + Postgres, or T3)
- Instrument observability across the stack
- Serve as the go-to person for small-team startups

The role in USA increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Full Stack Developer Salary Bands by Experience (USA, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (USD) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | $98K |
| Mid | 2–5 | $142K |
| Senior | 5–8 | $200K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | $275K |

Figures are total compensation (base + bonus + equity vest) pre-tax. Effective federal + state tax averages 28–37% depending on state.

## City-wise Full Stack Developer Salary in USA

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| San Francisco Bay Area | $132K | $192K | $270K |
| New York City | $118K | $170K | $240K |
| Seattle | $116K | $168K | $236K |
| Boston | $106K | $153K | $216K |
| Austin | $100K | $145K | $204K |
| Denver | $93K | $135K | $190K |
| Atlanta | $88K | $128K | $180K |

## Top Companies Hiring Full Stack Developers in USA (2027)

- **Google**
- **Meta**
- **Amazon**
- **Microsoft**
- **Apple**
- **Nvidia**
- **Netflix**
- **Stripe**
- **Databricks**
- **Anthropic**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Next.js + Server Actions
- Postgres + query tuning
- Type-safe APIs (tRPC, Zod)
- Edge deploys (Vercel, Cloudflare Workers)
- AI feature integration

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

US-remote roles typically pay 90–100% of Tier-2 metro comp; Bay Area on-site still commands the highest bands.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Junior FS (0–2 yr)**
2. **Full Stack Engineer (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior FS (4–7 yr)**
4. **Tech Lead (7–10 yr)**
5. **Fractional CTO / Founder-engineer (10+ yr)**

# Software Engineer Jobs in UK 2027: Average Salary, London vs Remote, IR35 & Big Tech Bands & Top Employers

> Software Engineer jobs in UK pay around £78K GBP mid-level in 2027. Explore London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands, top hiring firms, remote rates and negotiation tactics.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/software-engineer-salary-in-uk-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · UK


## Software Engineer Salary in UK 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Software Engineer** role in UK in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Software Engineer in UK in 2027 sits around **£78K GBP/year**. Entry £48K. Senior £125K. Staff/Lead £180K.

## What a Software Engineer Actually Does

- Design and implement production services (usually REST/gRPC APIs)
- Own code quality: reviews, tests, CI, observability
- Debug production incidents and contribute to postmortems
- Collaborate with PM/design to break epics into shippable slices

The role in UK increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Software Engineer Salary Bands by Experience (UK, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (GBP) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | £48K |
| Mid | 2–5 | £78K |
| Senior | 5–8 | £125K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | £180K |

Figures are gross base + typical bonus. UK income tax + NI cost 32–47% at these bands. Ltd-company contracting can shift the math.

## City-wise Software Engineer Salary in UK

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| London | £60K | £98K | £156K |
| Cambridge | £50K | £82K | £131K |
| Edinburgh | £47K | £76K | £123K |
| Manchester | £44K | £72K | £115K |
| Bristol | £46K | £74K | £119K |
| Leeds | £42K | £69K | £110K |
| Belfast | £39K | £64K | £103K |

## Top Companies Hiring Software Engineers in UK (2027)

- **Google DeepMind**
- **ARM**
- **Revolut**
- **Monzo**
- **Wise**
- **Deliveroo**
- **Ocado**
- **Meta London**
- **Amazon UK**
- **Cloudflare UK**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Distributed systems (Kafka, Kubernetes)
- Go or Rust for infra roles
- LLM integration (RAG, function calling)
- Security-first coding (OWASP, threat modeling)
- System design at scale

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

Fully-remote UK roles pay ~90% of London base but often ship equity of US parents at parity.

## Career Progression Path

1. **SWE I (0–2 yr)**
2. **SWE II (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior SWE (4–7 yr)**
4. **Staff SWE (7–10 yr)**
5. **Principal / Distinguished (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Software Engineer Salary in UK

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.

## FAQ

**Is Software Engineer still a good career in UK in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for Software Engineers in UK is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

**How long does it take to reach senior Software Engineer in UK?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

**Does remote work pay the same as on-site in UK?**
Usually within 5–15% of the metro band. Fully-remote roles from US-HQ employers often pay above local averages for non-US countries.

---

*Data compiled early 2027 from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow Dev Survey 2025, and LinkedIn Talent Insights. Individual offers vary; use this as a negotiation baseline, not a guarantee.*


## Why software engineer salary uk matters in 2027

Software Engineer jobs in UK pay around £78K GBP mid-level in 2027. Explore London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands, top hiring firms, remote rates and negotiation tactics. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · uk right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for software engineer salary uk filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is software engineer salary uk still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

### What should I do first?

Take the [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) if you are still choosing a direction, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) if you already have a target role and need to know what to learn next.

# QA Engineer Salary Guide — UK 2027: Bands, Bonuses, Equity & London vs Remote, IR35 & Big Tech Bands

> 2027 QA Engineer salary guide for UK: bands from £36K GBP to £125K GBP, London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands, in-demand skills and how to climb the career ladder faster.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/qa-engineer-salary-in-uk-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · UK


## QA Engineer Salary in UK 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **QA Engineer** role in UK in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level QA Engineer in UK in 2027 sits around **£58K GBP/year**. Entry £36K. Senior £88K. Staff/Lead £125K.

## What a QA Engineer Actually Does

- Design test strategy across unit, integration, and E2E layers
- Own automation suites (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, k6)
- Ship CI test pipelines and quality gates
- Champion accessibility and performance testing

The role in UK increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## QA Engineer Salary Bands by Experience (UK, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (GBP) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | £36K |
| Mid | 2–5 | £58K |
| Senior | 5–8 | £88K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | £125K |

Figures are gross base + typical bonus. UK income tax + NI cost 32–47% at these bands. Ltd-company contracting can shift the math.

## City-wise QA Engineer Salary in UK

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| London | £45K | £73K | £110K |
| Cambridge | £38K | £61K | £92K |
| Edinburgh | £35K | £57K | £86K |
| Manchester | £33K | £53K | £81K |
| Bristol | £34K | £55K | £84K |
| Leeds | £32K | £51K | £77K |
| Belfast | £30K | £48K | £72K |

## Top Companies Hiring QA Engineers in UK (2027)

- **Google DeepMind**
- **ARM**
- **Revolut**
- **Monzo**
- **Wise**
- **Deliveroo**
- **Ocado**
- **Meta London**
- **Amazon UK**
- **Cloudflare UK**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Playwright/Cypress at scale
- Performance testing (k6, JMeter, Gatling)
- Security testing (OWASP ZAP, Burp)
- Contract testing (Pact)
- SDET / test-in-production mindset

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

Fully-remote UK roles pay ~90% of London base but often ship equity of US parents at parity.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Junior QA (0–2 yr)**
2. **QA Engineer (2–4 yr)**
3. **SDET / Senior QA (4–7 yr)**
4. **QA Lead (7–10 yr)**
5. **Head of Quality (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your QA Engineer Salary in UK

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is data scientist salary uk still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

# DevOps Engineer Pay in UK (2027): London vs Remote, IR35 & Big Tech Bands and the Full Career-Ladder Breakdown

> DevOps Engineer pay in UK (2027): £85K GBP mid, £128K GBP senior. Career ladder, London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands and premium skills that command 20–35% higher offers.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/devops-engineer-salary-in-uk-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · UK


## DevOps Engineer Salary in UK 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **DevOps Engineer** role in UK in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level DevOps Engineer in UK in 2027 sits around **£85K GBP/year**. Entry £55K. Senior £128K. Staff/Lead £180K.

## What a DevOps Engineer Actually Does

- Design and operate CI/CD pipelines
- Run Kubernetes clusters, service mesh, observability stack
- Own IaC (Terraform, Pulumi) and cloud cost
- Lead incident response and SLO/error-budget practice

The role in UK increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## DevOps Engineer Salary Bands by Experience (UK, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (GBP) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | £55K |
| Mid | 2–5 | £85K |
| Senior | 5–8 | £128K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | £180K |

Figures are gross base + typical bonus. UK income tax + NI cost 32–47% at these bands. Ltd-company contracting can shift the math.

## City-wise DevOps Engineer Salary in UK

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| London | £69K | £106K | £160K |
| Cambridge | £58K | £89K | £134K |
| Edinburgh | £54K | £83K | £125K |
| Manchester | £51K | £78K | £118K |
| Bristol | £52K | £81K | £122K |
| Leeds | £48K | £75K | £113K |
| Belfast | £45K | £70K | £105K |

## Top Companies Hiring DevOps Engineers in UK (2027)

- **Google DeepMind**
- **ARM**
- **Revolut**
- **Monzo**
- **Wise**
- **Deliveroo**
- **Ocado**
- **Meta London**
- **Amazon UK**
- **Cloudflare UK**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- Kubernetes at multi-cluster scale
- Terraform + policy-as-code (OPA)
- eBPF / Cilium networking
- FinOps for cloud cost optimization
- Golang for internal tooling

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

Fully-remote UK roles pay ~90% of London base but often ship equity of US parents at parity.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Junior DevOps (0–2 yr)**
2. **DevOps Engineer (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior DevOps / SRE (4–7 yr)**
4. **Staff Platform Engineer (7–10 yr)**
5. **Principal / Head of Platform (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your DevOps Engineer Salary in UK

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## FAQ

**Is DevOps Engineer still a good career in UK in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for DevOps Engineers in UK is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

**How long does it take to reach senior DevOps Engineer in UK?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

**Does remote work pay the same as on-site in UK?**
Usually within 5–15% of the metro band. Fully-remote roles from US-HQ employers often pay above local averages for non-US countries.

## Why devops engineer salary uk matters in 2027

DevOps Engineer pay in UK (2027): £85K GBP mid, £128K GBP senior. Career ladder, London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands and premium skills that command 20–35% higher offers. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · uk right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for devops engineer salary uk filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

# Is Frontend Developer Worth It in UK in 2027? Salary Data, Demand & London vs Remote, IR35 & Big Tech Bands

> Should you pursue Frontend Developer in UK in 2027? Latest salary bands (£44K GBP–£155K GBP), demand trends and London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands — all in one guide.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/frontend-developer-salary-in-uk-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · UK


## Frontend Developer Salary in UK 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Frontend Developer** role in UK in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Frontend Developer in UK in 2027 sits around **£70K GBP/year**. Entry £44K. Senior £108K. Staff/Lead £155K.

## What a Frontend Developer Actually Does

- Build accessible, performant user interfaces (React/Next.js/Vue)
- Own component libraries and design-system tokens
- Ship Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse improvements
- Collaborate with design and product on UX quality

The role in UK increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Frontend Developer Salary Bands by Experience (UK, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (GBP) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | £44K |
| Mid | 2–5 | £70K |
| Senior | 5–8 | £108K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | £155K |

Figures are gross base + typical bonus. UK income tax + NI cost 32–47% at these bands. Ltd-company contracting can shift the math.

## City-wise Frontend Developer Salary in UK

Location still moves the needle by 25–40% even in a remote-friendly 2027 market.

| City | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|------|-------|-----|--------|
| London | £55K | £88K | £135K |
| Cambridge | £46K | £74K | £113K |
| Edinburgh | £43K | £69K | £106K |
| Manchester | £40K | £64K | £99K |
| Bristol | £42K | £67K | £103K |
| Leeds | £39K | £62K | £95K |
| Belfast | £36K | £57K | £89K |

## Top Companies Hiring Frontend Developers in UK (2027)

- **Google DeepMind**
- **ARM**
- **Revolut**
- **Monzo**
- **Wise**
- **Deliveroo**
- **Ocado**
- **Meta London**
- **Amazon UK**
- **Cloudflare UK**

Non-tech industries (banking, insurance, healthcare, defense) are the sleeper option — they often match FAANG base with better hours, especially at senior levels.

## Skills That Command a Premium in 2027

- React Server Components / Next.js 15
- TypeScript at scale
- Performance (Web Vitals, RUM)
- Accessibility (WCAG 2.2)
- Design-system engineering

Engineers who stack **one AI-adjacent skill** on top of their core specialty (e.g., a QA engineer who ships LLM evals, or a frontend dev who owns AI feature UX) are commanding 20–35% above the median band this year.

## Remote, Hybrid, and Contracting

Fully-remote UK roles pay ~90% of London base but often ship equity of US parents at parity.

## Career Progression Path

1. **Junior FE (0–2 yr)**
2. **Frontend Engineer (2–4 yr)**
3. **Senior FE (4–7 yr)**
4. **Staff UI Engineer (7–10 yr)**
5. **Principal FE / DS Lead (10+ yr)**

## How to Increase Your Frontend Developer Salary in UK

1. **Get a competing offer every 18–24 months** — the single biggest lever, worth 15–30% at each move.
2. **Specialize in a rising surface** — AI infra, platform, security, or data quality in 2027.
3. **Build public artifacts** — one strong OSS contribution or conference talk beats three certifications.
4. **Negotiate total comp, not base** — equity refresh, sign-on, and bonus targets are where offers actually differ.
5. **Track your levels** — use Levels.fyi and locality data before every conversation.

## FAQ

**Is Frontend Developer still a good career in UK in 2027?**
Yes. Even after the 2024–25 correction, demand for Frontend Developers in UK is up year-over-year, particularly at senior levels. Entry-level competition is tighter than in 2022, so a portfolio matters more than a degree.

**How long does it take to reach senior Frontend Developer in UK?**
5–7 years on average, faster (3–4 yr) at high-growth startups where scope is unlimited, slower at large enterprises.

**Does remote work pay the same as on-site in UK?**
Usually within 5–15% of the metro band. Fully-remote roles from US-HQ employers often pay above local averages for non-US countries.

## Why frontend developer salary uk matters in 2027

Should you pursue Frontend Developer in UK in 2027? Latest salary bands (£44K GBP–£155K GBP), demand trends and London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands — all in one guide. The context behind that has shifted quickly. Hiring in this area contracted for generalists after 2023 and expanded for specialists, which means the advice that worked five years ago — learn broadly, apply widely — now produces worse results than picking one area and going deep. Everything below is written with that in mind.

Three forces are shaping salary guide · uk right now: AI tooling raising the baseline of what one engineer can produce, distributed hiring widening the candidate pool for every posting, and employers weighting demonstrated output over credentials. Each of those cuts both ways — the bar is higher, but so is the ceiling for anyone with visible proof of work.

## Who this guide is for

- **Students and final-year candidates** deciding what to specialise in before graduating.
- **Career switchers** coming from non-technical or adjacent roles who need a realistic timeline, not a motivational one.
- **Working engineers** benchmarking their compensation and planning their next move.
- **Freelancers and contractors** setting rates against employed-market bands.

## What employers are actually screening for

Job descriptions are wish lists; screening criteria are much narrower. In practice a hiring loop for frontend developer salary uk filters on four things in order: does the CV show relevant, recent, measurable work; can the candidate reason out loud through an unfamiliar problem; do they understand the fundamentals underneath the tools they list; and can they communicate a trade-off to a non-specialist. Everything else — years of experience, degree, certification count — is a tiebreaker, not a gate.

How each stage is actually judged

| Stage | What they are testing | What passes | What fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CV screen | Relevance and evidence | Outcome bullets with numbers, keywords matched to the posting | Technology lists with no results attached |
| Recruiter call | Motivation and fit | A clear one-line story about why this role, this company | Vague answers and no questions asked back |
| Technical screen | Fundamentals under mild pressure | Thinking narrated out loud, clarifying questions first | Silent coding, then a wrong answer with no reasoning shown |
| Deep round | Depth and judgment | Concrete examples from real work, honest trade-offs | Textbook answers with no lived detail |
| Final / behavioural | Ownership and communication | Situation, action, measurable result | Blaming past teams or drifting off the question |

## Money: how to read a compensation range

A posted range is not a distribution — it is a budget. The midpoint is roughly what a well-prepared candidate at the expected level receives; the top of the band is reserved for people arriving with competing offers, unusual scope, or a scarce specialisation. That means the two levers that move your number are level and leverage, in that order. Negotiating five per cent inside a band is a smaller win than being hired one level higher, and the level is decided in the interview, not in the offer call.

- **Compare total compensation**, not base — bonus, equity, pension and benefits diverge sharply between company types.
- **Discount equity heavily** unless the company is public or you understand the strike price, vesting and liquidity terms.
- **Ask what band the role is budgeted at** rather than stating your expectation first.
- **Never negotiate from your previous salary** — anchor on the market band for the scope you are being hired for.
- **Take 48 hours** to review any written offer. It is standard and it does not put the offer at risk.

## Practical action plan

A 90-day plan you can start this week

| Weeks | Focus | Concrete output | How you know it worked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Baseline and target | A written target role, target band and gap list | You can name three specific skills to close |
| 3–6 | Close the biggest gap | One project that uses the missing skill in anger | It is deployed and someone other than you has used it |
| 7–10 | Proof and positioning | Rewritten CV, portfolio page, written case study | Your CV passes an ATS check and reads in outcomes |
| 11–13 | Market contact | 30 targeted applications, 5 referral conversations, weekly mocks | You are reaching final rounds, not just screens |

## What most people get wrong

1. Optimising for the highest advertised salary rather than the role they can sustain for three years.
2. Reading about the topic instead of producing something with it. Consumption feels like progress and rarely is.
3. Applying with an untailored CV, then concluding the market is closed.
4. Ignoring the fundamentals because the surface layer changes fast — the fundamentals are what interviews test.
5. Waiting for certainty. The information in this guide is enough to start; the rest is learned by doing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is frontend developer salary uk still worth pursuing in 2027?

Yes, with the caveat that generalist entry has become harder while specialist demand keeps rising. The realistic route is to pick one lane, build visible proof, and target employers whose stack you actually match.

### How long before I see results?

Skill-building shows up in three to six months; job-search results show up in six to twelve weeks of consistent, tailored applications. Both timelines assume weekly output rather than occasional bursts.

### How accurate are these salary figures?

They are market-band estimates compiled from public compensation datasets and job postings, expressed as annual gross. Treat them as a negotiating anchor rather than a guarantee — company type and scope move a band more than job title does.

### What should I do first?

Take the [free career quiz](https://www.skillta.tech/quiz) if you are still choosing a direction, or run the [skill gap analyzer](https://www.skillta.tech/skill-gap-analyzer) if you already have a target role and need to know what to learn next.

# Cybersecurity Analyst Salary in UK (2027): Entry-Level, Senior & Lead Pay — London vs Remote, IR35 & Big Tech Bands

> Complete 2027 Cybersecurity Analyst salary breakdown for UK: entry £52K GBP, mid £80K GBP, senior £122K GBP. City-wise pay, London vs regional pay, IR35 contractor day-rates and Big Tech UK bands, top employers & premium skills covered.

Canonical: https://www.skillta.tech/blog/cybersecurity-analyst-salary-in-uk-2026
Last updated: 2026-07-16

Published: 2026-07-16 · 11 min read · Salary Guide · UK


## Cybersecurity Analyst Salary in UK 2027 — At a Glance

If you are targeting a **Cybersecurity Analyst** role in UK in 2027, the market has shifted meaningfully since 2024. Post-2025 correction, salaries stabilized and roles tied to AI, cloud, and platform work rebounded fastest. Below is a full breakdown compiled from Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Payscale, Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, and live LinkedIn Talent Insights pulls for early 2027.

> **Quick answer:** the national average total comp for a mid-level Cybersecurity Analyst in UK in 2027 sits around **£80K GBP/year**. Entry £52K. Senior £122K. Staff/Lead £175K.

## What a Cybersecurity Analyst Actually Does

- Monitor SIEM/EDR and triage security incidents
- Run threat hunts and purple-team exercises
- Own vulnerability management and patch pipelines
- Support SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits

The role in UK increasingly overlaps with AI tooling — expect at least 20–30% of your workflow in 2027 to involve LLM copilots, agentic pipelines, or model-quality work regardless of your specialty.

## Cybersecurity Analyst Salary Bands by Experience (UK, 2027)

| Level | Years | Total Comp (GBP) |
|-------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Entry | 0–2 | £52K |
| Mid | 2–5 | £80K |
| Senior | 5–8 | £122K |
| Staff / Lead | 8+ | £175K |

Figures are gross base + typical bonus. UK income tax + NI cost 32–47% at these bands. Ltd-company contracting can shift the math.
